newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran starts building $1.5 bln gas refinery on Gulf.
newsitem.headline: Iran starts building $1.5 bln gas refinery on Gulf.

text.p: Iran has started construction work on a $1.5 billion refinery to treat gas from a large gas field in the Gulf, a newspaper said on Saturday.
The daily Kayhan said President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani on Friday launched the project to build the Siraf refinery for $900 million in hard cash as well as 960 billion rials ($549 million).
Rafsanjani said the refinery, near Iran's port of Bushehr on the northern Gulf, was Iran's "biggest industrial and economic project in the past and present", it added.
The project included exploration and excavation and the construction of rigs and pipelines to tranfer the gas from the South Pars field, 100 km (60 miles) from the coast, the newspaper said.
Iran said earlier in February the first phase of the project would come onstream in the second half of 1999 with an output of one billion cubic feet a day for domestic use.
The project is being handled by the Petroleum Development & Engineering Company, a subsidiary of the national Iranian Oil Company (NIOC), it said.
Further development of the field is vital for Iran's plans to export gas to Pakistan, India, Turkey and Europe in the next decade.
The NIOC has been in talks with a consortium led by Royal Dutch/Shell Group for the second phase development involving an additional one billion cubic feet a day of gas output.
France's Total recently said it was weighing the options of investing in the South Pars project.
South Pars is an extension in Iranian waters of Qatar's North Field.

The newsletter Middle East Economic Survey (MEES) said recently that the NIOC's offshore arm expected to revise estimates of the field's gas reserves to perhaps as much as 500 trillion cubic feet from 300 trillion cubic feet.
Iran has the world's second largest gas reserves after Russia. ($1=1,750 rials at the rate used for state budget accounts)
